## Overview

Adds opt-in layered prefill (`--num-layer-groups N`): a prefill batch advances one group of decoder layers per iteration, while running requests decode through all layers every iteration. Implements RFC #62689 ([paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.08055)).

## Claims

- New `SchedulerConfig.num_layer_groups` (default 1, off) for MRV2 with synchronous scheduling, supporting TP, PP and EP. With PP, each rank prefills its own batch, overlapping batches across ranks.
- Model-agnostic: any decoder following the PP contract (`layers[start_layer:end_layer]`, embed on first rank, `IntermediateTensors` before last) works without model changes. Unsupported models are rejected at load time.
- CUDA graphs: breakable prefill graphs per layer group, plus full decode graphs.
- On Qwen3-30B-A3B and GPT-OSS-20B (2× A100), SLO attainment improves at high load over chunked-512 and chunked-8192 (table below), with higher TTFT at light load.

## Validation

**Correctness.** Greedy tokens and logprobs match full-depth execution (`check_logprobs_close`), with and without prefix cache hits:

| Test | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `tests/distributed/test_pipeline_parallel.py -k layered` | 9 passed, 1 skipped (TP2+PP2 needs 4 GPUs) |
| `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler_e2e.py -k layered` | 4 passed, 2 skipped (4 GPUs) |
| `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -k layered`, `tests/test_config.py -k layered`, `tests/models/test_utils.py`, `tests/v1/cudagraph/`, `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py` | 808 passed, 5 skipped |
| `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` (groups 1, 4 with PP1; 4 with PP2) | 0 syncs detected |

The `test_pipeline_parallel` matrix covers:

- Qwen3-0.6B: PP1, PP2 (eager and graphs), TP2
- Llama-3.2-1B: PP2
- DeepSeek-V2-Lite: PP2, TP2+EP
- GPT-OSS-20B: PP2
- Qwen3-30B-A3B: TP2+EP, TP2+PP2+EP

TP2+PP2 needs 4 GPUs and was not run locally.

**Accuracy.** GSM8K (5-shot, 1319 questions, greedy) with Qwen3-30B-A3B, MRV2, synchronous scheduling, on the final commit:

| Config | Accuracy |
| --- | --- |
| chunked, TP2, 8192 tokens | 0.895 |
| layered, TP2, 16 groups, 8192 tokens | 0.898 |
| layered, PP2, 8 groups per rank, 4096 tokens | 0.887 |

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --num-layer-groups 16 --no-async-scheduling --no-enable-prefix-caching --max-model-len 4096
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --num-shots 5
```

**Serving.** `benchmarks/benchmark_layered_prefill.py`, 54 cases, 600 requests each, Poisson arrivals, seed 0, one run per case. Shown: SLO attainment / mean TTFT / p99 ITL. The SLO is TTFT 10 s (arXiv) or 5 s (ShareGPT), and every ITL ≤ 150 ms.

</details>

<details><summary>Reproduce</summary>

```bash
  --benchmark serve --output-dir layered-logs --gpus 0,1
```

</details>

## Details

- **Scheduler.** `LayeredPrefillScheduler` (new file) emits, per iteration:
  - one local stage per PP rank;
  - a full-depth decode batch;
  - the completed rows to sample.

  Partial prefill KV stays out of the prefix cache until every group has run (`delay_cache_blocks`).
- **Worker.** `LayeredPrefillRunner` (new file) handles retained activations, the PP send after the last local group, and a single sampling pass. Activation memory is reserved before KV cache sizing.
- **Models.** `layer_group_context` narrows `start_layer`/`end_layer` and the PP group's first/last flags, so each group runs as its own pipeline stage.
- **Breakable graph fix.** `eager_break_during_capture` decided at decoration time whether to wrap an op, but `VllmConfig` may auto-enable `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH` later.
  - If attention ops were imported first (e.g. `LLM(...)` in a process that already imported `vllm.model_executor.model_loader`), they were never breaks. Attention was then frozen into the graph: 0 eager breaks, with wrong outputs on DeepSeek-V2-Lite.
  - The decorator now always wraps; without an active capture the call passes through.
- **Limitations.**
  - Synchronous scheduling only; `torch.compile` is disabled.
  - Not supported: speculative decoding, DP, CP, DBO, EPLB, KV/EC connectors, multimodal and hybrid models.
  - The worker waits on a CUDA event two iterations back before reusing inputs. This wait falls within synchronous scheduling and was not flagged by `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK`.
- **Benchmark SLO.** The 150 ms TBT SLO replaces the paper's 100/125 ms, chosen after observing PP=2 results; `figure3.json` keeps the paper's values.
- **Duplicate check.** Searched open and closed PRs and issues for "layered prefill", "layer group prefill" and "num_layer_groups"; no existing work. Design discussed in RFC #62689.

+def read_config(config: dict) -> list[dict]:
+    """Expand each panel into paired schedules at the configured request rates."""
+    defaults = config["benchmark_defaults"]
+    parallelisms = config.get("parallelisms", {"default": {}})
+    rows = []
+    for panel in config["panels"]:
+        model = config["models"][panel["model"]]
+        for parallelism in panel.get("parallelisms", parallelisms):
+            for schedule, settings in config["schedules"].items():
+                mode = settings.get("mode", schedule)
+                if mode not in ("chunked-prefill", "layered-prefill"):
+                    raise ValueError(f"Unknown schedule mode: {mode}")
+                for rate in panel["request_rates"]:
+                    if rate <= 0:
+                        raise ValueError("Benchmark request rates must be positive")
+                    count = defaults["num_requests"]
+                    if "max_seconds" in defaults:
+                        count = min(count, int(defaults["max_seconds"] * rate))
+                    rows.append(
+                        {
+                            **config["engine_defaults"],
+                            **parallelisms[parallelism],
+                            **model,
+                            **settings,
+                            "panel": panel["id"],
+                            "parallelism": parallelism,
+                            "model_key": panel["model"],
+                            "schedule": schedule,
+                            "schedule_mode": mode,
+                            "num_layer_groups": model["num_layer_groups"]
+                            if mode == "layered-prefill"
+                            else 1,
+                            "dataset_name": panel["dataset"],
+                            "request_rate": rate,
+                            "burstiness": defaults["burstiness"],
+                            "num_requests": count,
+                            "ttft_slo_ms": panel["ttft_slo_ms"],
+                        }
+                    )
+    return rows

+def engine_config(row: dict, args: argparse.Namespace) -> dict:
+    source_model = row["model_name"]
+    model = source_model if Path(source_model).is_dir() else model_id(source_model)
+    config = {
+        "model": args.model or model,
+        "dtype": row["dtype"],
+        "max_num_batched_tokens": int(row["max_num_batched_tokens"]),
+        "max_num_seqs": int(row["max_num_seqs"]),
+        "max_model_len": int(row["max_model_len"]),
+        "gpu_memory_utilization": float(row["gpu_memory_utilization"]),
+        "tensor_parallel_size": args.tp or int(row["tensor_parallel_size"]),
+        "pipeline_parallel_size": args.pp or row["pipeline_parallel_size"],
+        "enable_expert_parallel": args.ep or row["enable_expert_parallel"],
+        "num_layer_groups": row["num_layer_groups"],
+        "distributed_executor_backend": "mp",
+        "enforce_eager": args.enforce_eager
+        or str(row["enforce_eager"]).lower() == "true",
+        "async_scheduling": False,
+        "enable_prefix_caching": False,
+        "enable_chunked_prefill": True,
+        "seed": args.seed,
+    }
+    if row["schedule_mode"] == "layered-prefill" and "layers_per_group" in row:
+        divisor = config["pipeline_parallel_size"] * row["layers_per_group"]
+        groups, remainder = divmod(row["num_hidden_layers"], divisor)
+        if remainder or groups < 2:
+            raise ValueError(
+                "PP must give each rank at least two complete layer groups"
+            )
+        config["num_layer_groups"] = groups
+    if row["schedule_mode"] == "layered-prefill":
+        # Each rank runs its own retained batch every tick, so split the budget.
+        pp = int(config["pipeline_parallel_size"])
+        config["max_num_batched_tokens"] //= pp
+    if not config["enforce_eager"]:
+        budget = config["max_num_batched_tokens"]
+        sizes = sorted({1 << i for i in range(budget.bit_length())} | {budget})
+        config["compilation_config"] = {
+            "mode": 0,
+            "cudagraph_mode": "FULL_AND_PIECEWISE",

+def sharegpt_requests(tokenizer, seed: int):
+    """Port of the reference ShareGPT sampler: repeated text, traced lengths."""
+    import datasets
+
+    data = datasets.load_dataset(
+        "Aeala/ShareGPT_Vicuna_unfiltered",
+        data_files={"valid": "ShareGPT_V4.3_unfiltered_cleaned_split.json"},
+        split="valid",
+    )
+    conversations = [
+        entry["conversations"]
+        for entry in data
+        if "conversations" in entry and len(entry["conversations"]) >= 2
+    ]
+    with urllib.request.urlopen(SHAREGPT_LENGTHS_URL, timeout=60) as response:
+        trace = response.read()
+    if hashlib.sha256(trace).hexdigest() != SHAREGPT_LENGTHS_SHA256:
+        raise RuntimeError(f"Unexpected ShareGPT length trace: {SHAREGPT_LENGTHS_URL}")
+    lengths = [
+        (int(row["num_prefill_tokens"]), int(row["num_decode_tokens"]))
+        for row in csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(trace.decode()))
+    ]
+    lengths = [(i, o) for i, o in lengths if i > 0 and o > 0]
+    random.seed(seed)
+    random.shuffle(conversations)
+    random.shuffle(lengths)
+
+    roles = {"human": "user", "gpt": "assistant"}
+
+    def role(sentence: dict) -> str:
+        return roles[sentence["from"]] if "from" in sentence else sentence["role"]
+
+    key = "value" if "value" in conversations[0][0] else "content"
+    num_special_tokens = tokenizer.num_special_tokens_to_add()
+    index = 0
+    for input_len, output_len in lengths:
+        while True:
+            # The reference sampler skips conversations[0].
+            index += 1
+            entry = conversations[index]
+            if role(entry[0]) != "user":
+                entry = entry[1:]
+            messages = []
+            for _ in range(10):
+                for j, sentence in enumerate(entry):
+                    assert role(sentence) == ("user", "assistant")[j % 2]
+                    # In place, as in the reference: repeats accumulate spaces.
+                    if role(sentence) == "assistant":
+                        sentence[key] = " " + sentence[key]
+                    messages.append({"role": role(sentence), "content": sentence[key]})
+            prompt = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
+                messages[:-1], tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True
+            )
+            token_ids = tokenizer.encode(prompt, add_special_tokens=False)
+            token_ids = token_ids[: input_len - num_special_tokens]
+            if len(token_ids) >= input_len:
+                yield tokenizer.decode(token_ids), output_len
+                break
+

+def arxiv_requests(tokenizer):
+    """Port of the reference arXiv sampler, in dataset order from data[0]."""
+    import datasets
+
+    for entry in datasets.load_dataset("ccdv/arxiv-summarization", split="test"):
+        messages = [
+            {
+                "role": "user",
+                "content": entry["article"] + "\n\nSummarize the above article.\n\n",
+            }
+        ]
+        prompt = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
+            messages, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True
+        )
+        yield prompt, len(tokenizer.encode(entry["abstract"], add_special_tokens=False))
+

+def sample_dataset(
+    candidates, tokenizer, name: str, count: int, max_model_len: int
+) -> tuple[list[dict], int]:
+    """Select full requests that fit, advancing past oversized requests."""
+    requests = []
+    skipped = 0
+    for prompt, output_length in candidates:
+        length = len(tokenizer(prompt).input_ids)
+        if length + output_length > max_model_len:
+            skipped += 1
+            continue
+        requests.append({"prompt": prompt, "output_tokens": output_length})
+        if len(requests) == count:
+            return requests, skipped
+    raise ValueError(
+        f"Expected {count} valid {name} requests, got {len(requests)}; "
+        f"skipped {skipped} exceeding max_model_len={max_model_len} "
+        "(prompt + output tokens). Source samples exhausted."
+    )
+

+def prepare_datasets(cases: list[dict], args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
+    from transformers import AutoTokenizer
+
+    grouped = defaultdict(list)
+    for case in cases:
+        grouped[dataset_file(args.output_dir, case)].append(case)
+    for path, group in grouped.items():
+        if path.exists():
+            continue
+        case = group[0]
+        name = case["workload"]["dataset"]
+        if name not in ("arxiv", "sharegpt"):
+            raise ValueError(f"Unsupported source dataset: {name}")
+        tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(
+            case["engine"]["model"], revision=case["engine"].get("revision")
+        )
+        candidates = (
+            arxiv_requests(tokenizer)
+            if name == "arxiv"
+            else sharegpt_requests(tokenizer, args.seed)
+        )
+        count = max(c["workload"]["num_prompts"] for c in group)
+        max_model_len = min(c["engine"]["max_model_len"] for c in group)
+        requests, skipped = sample_dataset(
+            candidates, tokenizer, name, count, max_model_len
+        )
+        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+        temporary = path.with_suffix(".tmp")
+        with temporary.open("w") as file:
+            for request in requests:
+                file.write(json.dumps(request) + "\n")
+        write_json(
+            path.with_suffix(".metadata.json"),
+            {
+                "model": case["engine"]["model"],
+                "dataset": name,
+                "seed": args.seed,
+                "max_model_len": max_model_len,
+                "num_requests": len(requests),
+                "skipped_over_context": skipped,
+            },
+        )
+        temporary.replace(path)
+        print(
+            f"Prepared {len(requests)} {name} requests for {case['engine']['model']}; "
+            f"skipped {skipped} over context limit {max_model_len}. Dataset: {path}",
+            flush=True,
+        )

+@contextlib.contextmanager
+def process(command: list[str], log: Path, env: dict):
+    with log.open("w") as file:
+        child = subprocess.Popen(
+            command,
+            stdout=file,
+            stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
+            env=env,
+            cwd=ROOT,
+            start_new_session=True,
+        )
+        try:
+            yield child
+        finally:
+            # The process group belongs to this invocation, including its workers.
+            with contextlib.suppress(ProcessLookupError):
+                os.killpg(child.pid, signal.SIGTERM)
+            with contextlib.suppress(subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
+                child.wait(timeout=10)
+            with contextlib.suppress(ProcessLookupError):
+                os.killpg(child.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
+            child.wait()
+

+def run_command(command: list[str], log: Path, env: dict, timeout: int) -> None:
+    print(shlex.join(command), flush=True)
+    with process(command, log, env) as child:
+        code = child.wait(timeout=timeout)
+        if code:
+            raise RuntimeError(f"Command exited with {code}; see {log}")
+

+def wait_for_server(child: subprocess.Popen, port: int, timeout: int) -> None:
+    deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
+    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
+        if child.poll() is not None:
+            raise RuntimeError("Server exited during startup; see server.log")
+        try:
+            with urllib.request.urlopen(
+                f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}/health", timeout=2
+            ) as response:
+                if response.status == 200:
+                    return
+        except (urllib.error.URLError, TimeoutError):
+            pass
+        time.sleep(1)
+    raise TimeoutError("Server readiness timed out; see server.log")

+def paper_slo_metrics(result: dict, workload: dict) -> dict:
+    """Apply Table 5 to each request, including its worst inter-token latency."""
+    count = workload["num_prompts"]
+    ttfts, itls = result["ttfts"], result["itls"]
+    errors, lengths = result["errors"], result["output_lens"]
+    if not all(len(values) == count for values in (ttfts, itls, errors, lengths)):
+        raise ValueError("Incomplete per-request timings for Figure 3 SLO evaluation")
+    ttft_passed = tbt_passed = both_passed = 0
+    for ttft, intervals, error, length in zip(ttfts, itls, errors, lengths):
+        if error or length <= 0:
+            continue
+        if length > 1 and not intervals:
+            raise ValueError("Missing inter-token timings for a multi-token response")
+        meets_ttft = 0 <= ttft * 1000 <= workload["ttft_slo_ms"]
+        meets_tbt = all(0 <= t * 1000 <= workload["tbt_slo_ms"] for t in intervals)
+        ttft_passed += meets_ttft
+        tbt_passed += meets_tbt
+        both_passed += meets_ttft and meets_tbt
+    return {
+        "slo_attained": both_passed,
+        "slo_attainment_pct": 100 * both_passed / count,
+        "ttft_attainment_pct": 100 * ttft_passed / count,
+        "tbt_attainment_pct": 100 * tbt_passed / count,
+    }
+

+def run_case(case: dict, args: argparse.Namespace, env: dict, port: int = 8000) -> None:
+    directory = args.output_dir / case["id"]
+    directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    status = directory / "status.json"
+    if args.resume and is_complete(directory):
+        print(f"Skipping completed {case['id']}", flush=True)
+        return
+    write_json(status, {"status": "running", "case": case})
+    try:
+        if args.benchmark == "serve" and int(
+            args.warmup_seconds * case["workload"]["request_rate"]
+        ):
+            run_command(
+                benchmark_command(case, args, port, warmup=True),
+                directory / "warmup.log",
+                env,
+                args.timeout,
+            )
+        command = benchmark_command(case, args, port)
+        write_json(directory / "command.json", command)
+        (directory / "result.json").unlink(missing_ok=True)
+        run_command(command, directory / "benchmark.log", env, args.timeout)
+        result = json.loads((directory / "result.json").read_text())
+        if (
+            args.benchmark == "serve"
+            and result["completed"] != case["workload"]["num_prompts"]
+        ):
+            errors = [
+                f"request[{i}]: {error.strip().splitlines()[-1]}"
+                for i, error in enumerate(result.get("errors", []))
+                if error and error.strip()
+            ]
+            detail = "; ".join(errors[:3]) or "No per-request error recorded"
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                f"Only {result['completed']} requests completed out of "
+                f"{case['workload']['num_prompts']}; {detail}. "
+                f"See {directory / 'result.json'}"
+            )
+        if args.benchmark == "serve":
+            result.update(paper_slo_metrics(result, case["workload"]))
+            write_json(directory / "result.json", result)
+        write_json(status, {"status": "ok", "case": case})
+    except Exception as error:
+        write_json(status, {"status": "failed", "case": case, "error": str(error)})
+        raise

+            "parallelism": ",".join(

+            ),
+            "schedule": ",".join(dict.fromkeys(s["schedule"] for s in case["sources"])),
+            **case["engine"],
+            **case["workload"],
+            "status": status["status"],
+        }
+        if status["status"] == "ok":
+            result = json.loads((directory / "result.json").read_text())
+            row.update(
+                {
+                    key: value
+                    for key, value in result.items()
+                    if key
+                    in {
+                        "avg_latency",
+                        "completed",
+                        "duration",
+                        "request_throughput",
+                        "output_throughput",
+                        "total_token_throughput",
+                        "slo_attained",
+                        "slo_attainment_pct",
+                        "ttft_attainment_pct",

+# Layered Prefill
+
+Layered prefill splits the decoder layers on each pipeline rank into groups and
+advances a prefill batch through one group per engine iteration, instead of
+splitting prompts into token chunks. Every iteration also runs a full-depth
+decode step for the running requests, so a long prompt delays each decode step
+by one group instead of the whole model.
+
+Compared with chunked prefill, each prompt token passes through every layer
+once with a large batch. For MoE models this avoids reloading expert weights
+for every chunk, and it keeps inter-token latency bounded while prompts are
+being prefilled.
+
+See: [Layered Prefill paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.08055)
+
+## Usage
+
+```bash
+vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B \
+    --num-layer-groups 16 \
+    --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
+    --no-async-scheduling
+```
+
+`--num-layer-groups` is the number of groups per pipeline rank and must not
+exceed the number of layers on any rank. A prompt completes prefill after
+`num_layer_groups × pipeline_parallel_size` iterations. With PP, each rank runs
+its own prefill batch every iteration, so a new batch can start while earlier
+batches finish on downstream ranks.
+
+## Requirements and limitations
+
+- Model Runner V2 and synchronous scheduling (`--no-async-scheduling`).
+  `torch.compile` is disabled; CUDA graphs use breakable prefill graphs for
+  each layer group and full graphs for decode.
+- Text-only generation models whose decoder iterates
+  `layers[start_layer:end_layer]` with the standard pipeline-parallel interface.
+  This covers most models that support pipeline parallelism.
+- TP, PP and EP are supported. Speculative decoding, data and context
+  parallelism, DBO, EPLB, KV/encoder transfer connectors, and hybrid or
+  attention-free models are not yet supported.
+- The `mp` or `uni` executor backend.
+

+from collections.abc import Iterator
+from contextlib import contextmanager
+from typing import Any
+from weakref import WeakKeyDictionary
+
+from torch import nn
+
+import vllm.distributed.parallel_state as parallel_state
+
+_decoders: WeakKeyDictionary[nn.Module, nn.Module] = WeakKeyDictionary()
+
+
+def get_layer_group_range(
+    start_layer: int, end_layer: int, group_idx: int, num_groups: int
+) -> tuple[int, int]:
+    """Split the local PP partition into contiguous, nonempty groups."""
+    num_layers = end_layer - start_layer
+    if not 0 <= group_idx < num_groups <= num_layers:
+        raise ValueError("Layer groups must be nonempty and lie within the PP rank.")
+    size, remainder = divmod(num_layers, num_groups)
+    start = start_layer + group_idx * size + min(group_idx, remainder)
+    return start, start + size + (group_idx < remainder)
+
+
+def get_layered_decoder(model: nn.Module) -> nn.Module:
+    """Return the module whose forward iterates `layers[start_layer:end_layer]`.
+
+    Every model that supports PP this way can run local layer groups: a group
+    is executed as if it were its own pipeline stage.
+    """
+    decoder = _decoders.get(model)
+    if decoder is None:
+        candidates = [
+            module
+            for module in model.modules()
+            if isinstance(getattr(module, "layers", None), nn.ModuleList)
+            and isinstance(getattr(module, "start_layer", None), int)
+            and isinstance(getattr(module, "end_layer", None), int)
+        ]
+        if len(candidates) != 1:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"Layered prefill requires {type(model).__name__} to contain one "
+                "decoder with `layers`, `start_layer` and `end_layer`; found "
+                f"{len(candidates)}."
+            )
+        decoder = _decoders[model] = candidates[0]
+    return decoder
+
+
+class _PPGroupView:
+    def __init__(self, group: Any, is_first_rank: bool, is_last_rank: bool):
+        self._group = group
+        self.is_first_rank = is_first_rank
+        self.is_last_rank = is_last_rank
+
+    def __getattr__(self, name: str) -> Any:
+        return getattr(self._group, name)
+
+
+@contextmanager
+def layer_group_context(
+    model: nn.Module, group_idx: int | None, num_groups: int
+) -> Iterator[None]:
+    """Run only one local layer group of `model`, or all layers if None.
+
+    The decoder's layer range is narrowed and the PP group reports stage
+    boundaries at the group, so the model embeds only before the first group
+    and returns intermediate tensors before the last.
+    """
+    if group_idx is None:
+        yield
+        return
+    decoder = get_layered_decoder(model)
+    pp = parallel_state.get_pp_group()
+    full_range = decoder.start_layer, decoder.end_layer
+    start, end = get_layer_group_range(*full_range, group_idx, num_groups)
+    decoder.start_layer, decoder.end_layer = start, end

+        pp,
+        is_first_rank=pp.is_first_rank and group_idx == 0,
+        is_last_rank=pp.is_last_rank and group_idx == num_groups - 1,
+    )

+    traversing the pipeline, its requests cannot be preempted or rescheduled.
